    const { z } = require('zod');
    const { READ_TURN_LIMITS, providerToolCallSchema } = require('./read-turn.validator');
    const { proposalSchema } = require('./proposal.validator');
    
    const CONVERSATION_LIMITS = Object.freeze({
      turns: 8,
      recordBytes: READ_TURN_LIMITS.conversationBytes + 4096,
      redisTimeoutMs: 1000,
    });
    
    const userMessageSchema = z.object({
      role: z.literal('user'),
      content: z.string().min(1).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.messageChars).refine((value) => Boolean(value.trim())),
    }).strict();
    const assistantMessageSchema = z.object({
      role: z.literal('assistant'),
      content: z.string().min(1).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.replyChars).refine((value) => Boolean(value.trim())),
    }).strict();
    const assistantCallsSchema = z.object({
      role: z.literal('assistant'),
      content: z.string().max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.replyChars).nullable(),
      tool_calls: z.array(z.object({
        id: providerToolCallSchema.shape.id,
        type: z.literal('function'),
        function: z.object({
          name: providerToolCallSchema.shape.name,
          arguments: providerToolCallSchema.shape.arguments,
        }).strict(),
      }).strict()).min(1).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolCalls),
    }).strict();
    const toolMessageSchema = z.object({
      role: z.literal('tool'),
      tool_call_id: providerToolCallSchema.shape.id,
      content: z.string().max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolResultBytes).refine((value) => {
        if (Buffer.byteLength(value, 'utf8') > READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolResultBytes) return false;
        try {
          const envelope = JSON.parse(value);
          return envelope?.kind === 'untrusted_tool_result' && Object.hasOwn(envelope, 'data')
            && Object.keys(envelope).length === 2;
        } catch { return false; }
      }, 'Invalid tool result envelope'),
    }).strict();
    
    // Store only completed turns. Incomplete calls and system/developer messages
    // can never be restored into a later request, even from a corrupt Redis record.
    const turnSchema = z.array(z.union([
      userMessageSchema, assistantMessageSchema, assistantCallsSchema, toolMessageSchema,
    ])).min(4).max(2 + READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolCalls * 2).refine((messages) => {
      if (messages[0]?.role !== 'user' || messages.at(-1)?.role !== 'assistant' || messages.at(-1).tool_calls) return false;
      const ids = new Set();
      let index = 1;
      while (index < messages.length - 1) {
        const message = messages[index++];
        if (message.role !== 'assistant' || !message.tool_calls) return false;
        for (const call of message.tool_calls) {
          if (ids.has(call.id)) return false;
          ids.add(call.id);
          const result = messages[index++];
          if (result?.role !== 'tool' || result.tool_call_id !== call.id) return false;
        }
      }
      return index === messages.length - 1 && ids.size <= READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolCalls;
    }, 'Invalid completed conversation turn');
    
    const historySchema = z.array(turnSchema).max(CONVERSATION_LIMITS.turns)
      .refine((turns) => Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(turns), 'utf8') <= READ_TURN_LIMITS.conversationBytes,
        'Conversation history is too large');
    const conversationRecordSchema = z.object({
      version: z.literal(1),
      scope: z.string().regex(/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/),
      turns: historySchema,
    }).strict();
    const conversationResultSchema = z.object({
      reply: z.object({
        text: assistantMessageSchema.shape.content,
        modelCalls: z.number().int().min(1).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.modelCalls),
        toolCalls: z.number().int().min(1).max(READ_TURN_LIMITS.toolCalls),
        proposal: proposalSchema.optional(),
      }).strict(),
      history: historySchema,
    }).strict().refine(({ reply, history }) => history.length > 0 && history.at(-1)?.at(-1)?.content === reply.text,
      'Conversation reply does not match its history');
    
    const acquireReplySchema = z.union([
      z.tuple([z.literal('ready'), z.string().max(CONVERSATION_LIMITS.recordBytes)]),
      z.tuple([z.enum(['missing', 'busy', 'exists'])]),
    ]);
    const commitReplySchema = z.tuple([z.enum(['saved', 'missing', 'lost'])]);
    
    module.exports = {
      CONVERSATION_LIMITS, historySchema, conversationRecordSchema, conversationResultSchema,
      acquireReplySchema, commitReplySchema,
    };
    const { success } = require('../../utils/response');
    const audit = require('../../services/audit.service');
    const { decideProposal, getProposalStatus } = require('../services/proposal.service');
    const { emptyApprovalSchema, proposalIdSchema } = require('../validators/proposal.validator');
    
    const decision = (action) => async (req, res, next) => {
      try {
        const result = await decideProposal({
          context: { userId: req.user.id, member: req.member, workspace: req.workspace, requestId: req.requestId },
          proposalId: proposalIdSchema.parse(req.params.proposalId), data: emptyApprovalSchema.parse(req.body),
          decision: action, actorCtx: audit.fromReq(req),
        });
        res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
        success(res, result);
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    };
    
    async function status(req, res, next) {
      try {
        const result = await getProposalStatus({
          context: { userId: req.user.id, member: req.member, workspace: req.workspace, requestId: req.requestId },
          proposalId: proposalIdSchema.parse(req.params.proposalId),
        });
        res.set('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
        success(res, result);
      } catch (err) { next(err); }
    }
    
    module.exports = { approve: decision('approve'), reject: decision('reject'), status };
    // Mounted only inside workspace.routes, after auth and active membership.
    const router = require('express').Router({ mergeParams: true });
    const { agentLimiter } = require('../../middleware/rateLimiter');
    const { chat } = require('../controllers/chat.controller');
    const { approve, reject, status } = require('../controllers/proposal.controller');
    
    router.post('/chat', agentLimiter, chat);
    router.get('/proposals/:proposalId', agentLimiter, status);
    router.post('/proposals/:proposalId/approve', agentLimiter, approve);
    router.post('/proposals/:proposalId/reject', agentLimiter, reject);
    
    module.exports = router;

    # Notification proposals
    
    The first agent write is Tier 2 `mark_notification_read`: one notification
    belonging to the caller in the current workspace. The backend requires target
    selection, a proposal, and a separate approval request. Chat text and model
    tool calls cannot execute the write. Other writes remain unavailable.
    
    ## Select and propose
    
    After the user explicitly selects a notification in their workspace inbox,
    send its ID with the chat message:
    
    ```json
    {
      "message": "Mark the selected notification as read.",
      "selected_notification_id": "<notification-uuid>",
      "conversation_id": null
    }
    ```
    
    Use the existing authenticated `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/chat`.
    The server rereads active membership and the notification. Another recipient's
    notification, another workspace's notification and missing notifications return
    the same not-found response. An already-read selection is rejected. Fresh
    membership checks reject role changes, removed memberships and deleted
    workspaces even if the HTTP membership cache is stale.
    
    Only this selected request offers `mark_notification_read` to the model. Its
    arguments must be `{}`: the model cannot choose or change an ID. A UUID in
    chat text is not a selection, and selection is never inherited from history.
    Until a general selection flow exists, clients must obtain explicit selection
    separately; the backend does not guess from titles or partial lists.
    
    When requested by the model, the server rereads the notification, persists
    and audits a proposal, then ends the turn. A proposal tool call must appear
    alone, not in a batch of reads or proposals. Chat can also return a normal
    text reply without proposing anything.
    
    The response's existing `data` object gains `proposal`:
    
    ```json
    {
      "id": "<proposal-uuid>",
      "tool": "mark_notification_read",
      "tier": 2,
      "summary": "Mark the selected notification as read.",
      "parameters": { "notification_id": "<notification-uuid>" },
      "before": {
        "id": "<notification-uuid>",
        "type": "task.assigned",
        "title": "Your task is ready",
        "is_read": false,
        "read_at": null,
        "created_at": "2026-11-09T12:00:00.000Z"
      },
      "after": { "is_read": true },
      "expires_at": "<server-generated-ISO-timestamp>"
    }
    ```
    
    The title is untrusted display text. Summary and before/after fields come from
    server code and domain reads, not model prose. Notification bodies, delivery
    data, recipient IDs and audit request metadata are excluded from the card.
    For SSE, the card appears in `done.data.proposal`, after conversation storage
    when requested. A partial stream is neither a proposal receipt nor approval.
    Frontend selection and approval controls are not part of this backend change.
    
    ## Approve or reject
    
    Send a distinct authenticated POST with an empty JSON body `{}` to:
    
    ```text
    POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/proposals/:proposalId/approve
    POST /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/proposals/:proposalId/reject
    ```
    
    Both routes share the agent's per-user request limiter and never call the
    model. They reject parameter, identity, tier and tool overrides. Approval uses
    the saved parameters, rereads membership, audits the approval, verifies the
    preview and performs a conditional domain-service update. Changes to the
    reviewed title/type/date/read state invalidate the proposal. Concurrent
    updates cannot rewrite an existing read timestamp through this path.
    
    Approval returns `{ data: { proposal_id, status: "executed", result } }`.
    The result contains `notification_id`, `is_read: true` and the database's
    stored `read_at`. Rejection returns `{ data: { proposal_id, status: "rejected" } }`.
    Repeated successful decisions return the saved receipt; an opposite decision
    returns a conflict. Display the decision beside its proposal. Approval does
    not call the model or append a conversation turn; later chat must refresh
    notification facts through reads. Saying “approve” in chat cannot execute it.
    Disconnecting after submitting approval does not revoke it; retry the same
    proposal ID to learn its outcome rather than creating a replacement action.
    
    ## Expiry, failures and audit
    
    Pending approval expires five minutes after issuance. Redis retains records
    and receipts for 24 hours from issuance, bound to the exact user, membership,
    workspace and role. Commands have a one-second deadline. Missing/differently
    scoped IDs return `AGENT_PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND` (404); expired approvals return
    `AGENT_PROPOSAL_EXPIRED` (410). Corrupt/unavailable storage returns
    `AGENT_PROPOSAL_UNAVAILABLE` (503). There is no memory fallback or rebuilding
    of a missing proposal from client data.
    
    Atomic comparisons serialize decisions. `AGENT_PROPOSAL_BUSY` (409) means
    another transition won; retry the same decision to check its outcome.
    `AGENT_PROPOSAL_STALE` (409) means the notification changed and needs a new
    selection/proposal. A conditional database conflict applies no write.
    `AGENT_PROPOSAL_INDETERMINATE` (409) means the result is unknown: check the
    actual notification before starting another action. Execution claims are
    never reclaimed to repeat mutations after a crash or lost acknowledgement.
    
    Proposal, approval, execution and rejection events use `audit.log` and the
    new `AUDIT_ACTIONS` entries. Metadata identifies the proposal, turn, tool,
    tier, exact parameters and agent origin. `audit.fromReq` supplies HTTP actor
    metadata; identity stays pinned to authenticated context. Notification text
    is not copied into audit metadata. Stable audit UUIDs use insert-only conflict
    handling, preserving the append-only table without duplicating retry events.
    
    Required auditing fails closed before execution. If a successful result was
    saved but final auditing failed, repeating approval completes the audit and
    returns the receipt without rerunning the write. Failure audit metadata
    distinguishes unknown execution outcomes. If result storage fails, execution
    auditing is still attempted and the API reports uncertainty. Redis and
    Postgres do not share a transaction: a crash or outage can leave an unresolved
    claim or missing completion audit. This first path relies on a conditional
    notification update; broader writes need their own durable guarantees.
    
    Existing notification HTTP calls and ordinary audit callers retain their
    default behavior. New service options are internal and cannot be set through
    model or approval input. No schema changes are required.
    
    Unit tests cover scoped handlers, real HTTP composition with mocked services,
    Redis scripts, races, stale snapshots, audit recovery and uncertain writes.
    `tests/integration/database/notification-proposals.test.js` covers real
    membership joins, conditional updates and append-only audit deduplication;
    it requires the Postgres/PostgREST/Redis test stack and has not been run here.
    Live-model proposal behavior and deployed Redis recovery remain evaluation
    and integration work.
    # Agent tools
    
    This module currently provides read tools through `getAvailableTools(context)`
    and `executeReadTool({ name, args, context })`. Server code must build context
    after the existing auth and membership middleware:
    
    ```js
    const context = { userId: req.user.id, member: req.member, workspace: req.workspace, requestId: req.requestId };
    ```
    
    The registry includes all seven Tier 0 tools and all 28 Tier 1 tool names
    from the architecture, with the role restrictions and data limits documented
    below. Ranked task, ledger, dispute and group searches implement the
    [approved schema extension](SEARCH_SCHEMA_PROPOSAL.md).
    Chat supports JSON replies, opt-in SSE streaming, and a
    [notification proposal/approval flow](PROPOSALS.md). Other writes and voice
    are still pending.
    
    `find_member`, `find_container`, `find_disputes` and `find_group` take
    `{ query, limit? }`. `find_tasks` and `find_ledger_entries` also accept an
    optional resolved `container_id` UUID. Queries are trimmed and must contain
    2–200 characters; limits default to 10 and range from 2 to 20. Workspace,
    actor IDs and admin flags are always supplied by server context.
    
    Results contain `query`, `status`, `candidates`, and `has_more`. Candidates are
    ranked in PostgreSQL: exact matches, literal substrings, then trigram matches,
    with score/text/ID tie-breakers. `score` is a similarity value, not a probability.
    Member lookup excludes inactive/deleted members; container lookup includes
    archived/completed containers but excludes deleted ones. Both exclude deleted
    workspaces; the other search scopes are described below.
    
    - `not_found`: no candidates.
    - `single_match`: one candidate to confirm with the user before a write.
    - `ambiguous`: multiple candidates; the user must choose or refine the query.
    
    No result contains an automatically resolved ID. Write proposals must enforce
    the user's entity selection separately from action approval; the notification
    flow requires an explicit client selection for the current request.
    `has_more` means further candidates were omitted; refine the query or increase
    the limit. All returned names, titles, notes, reasons and descriptions remain
    untrusted data.
    
    ## Task, ledger, dispute and group resolution
    
    The four additional Tier 0 tools use the shared ranked-search service and
    PostgreSQL RPCs. Their handlers independently check active membership and
    strictly validate arguments, including direct handler calls. Identity and
    role overrides are rejected before a service call.
    
    | Tool | Matches | Member visibility |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `find_tasks` | Task title | Tasks assigned to the caller |
    | `find_ledger_entries` | Note, contributor name, exact original amount | Entries contributed by the caller |
    | `find_disputes` | Reason, raiser name, linked ledger note | Disputes raised by the caller |
    | `find_group` | Group name | Group directory metadata |
    
    Admins may search workspace tasks, entries and disputes. The private-data
    RPCs also recheck active, non-deleted membership in the requested workspace;
    broader access requires both the supplied admin flag and the current database
    admin role. A stale admin flag cannot elevate a member. All searches exclude
    deleted workspaces. Task/ledger searches exclude deleted containers, and task
    search excludes deleted tasks. Disputes remain searchable as historical
    records after container deletion. Joined names and ledger notes are scoped
    to the same workspace. Group search does not grant access to the admin-only
    `get_group` tool.
    
    Ledger amount queries must be plain signed decimals, with at most two decimal
    places. SQL compares them as `numeric` and returns original amounts as decimal
    text, preserving precision and each entry's currency. For a one-digit amount,
    use a query such as `5.00` to meet the two-character minimum. Currency symbols,
    commas, scientific notation and natural-language amounts are not interpreted
    as amounts. This search does not convert currencies, infer dates or calculate
    totals; the same amount in different currencies can yield separate candidates.
    
    Candidates provide the IDs and metadata needed for clarification, without
    proofs, bulk exports, internal actor fields or embedded membership/note arrays.
    Use selected task/entry IDs and their container IDs with `get_task` or
    `get_ledger_entry`; use a selected dispute ID with `get_dispute`. Exact matches
    still remain ambiguous when other candidates exist. Failures return
    `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`, not a false no-match. The read loop keeps results in
    untrusted-data envelopes and prevents direct write execution and bulk exports.
    
    ## Container browsing
    
    `list_containers` and `get_container` are Tier 1 reads available to active
    members and admins, matching the existing container HTTP routes. Both use
    the authenticated workspace and exclude deleted containers. Handlers check
    membership themselves; model arguments cannot change identity, include
    deleted records, or select a broader service view.
    
    Lists accept optional `type` (`event` or `recurring`), stored `status`
    (`active`, `completed`, or `archived`), and `sort` (`created_at`, `name`, or
    `event_date`, with an optional leading `-` for descending order). The default
    is ascending creation date with an ID tie-breaker. `page` ranges from 1 to
    10,000 and `per_page` from 1 to 100 (defaults: 1 and 20). Filtered totals and
    `next_page` come from the server; the model must not count list rows. A null
    next page means the end of the results or the page limit.
    
    List results contain identity/type/status, subtitle, task/money enablement,
    stored event/recurrence dates, and lifecycle timestamps. `get_container`
    accepts only a resolved `container_id` UUID and adds description, event type,
    recurrence settings, the stored budget target/currency, completion notes,
    and the source container ID after a conversion. Budget targets are settings,
    not collected/remaining balances; the agent must not calculate totals or
    future billing dates. Use `get_container_summary` for permitted financial
    and participant summaries and `list_cycles` for admin billing schedules.
    
    Use `find_container` for names and clarify ambiguous matches. A partial list
    cannot establish that a name is unique. All user-written text remains in the
    untrusted-data envelope. Neither tool exposes public-link tokens, files,
    ledger rows, participant/cycle records, or internal actor fields.
    
    The existing container service supports internal paginated metadata lists
    and a `metadataOnly` detail view, avoiding those unrelated joins and reads.
    Existing HTTP callers keep their unpaginated list/detail envelopes. Failed
    base queries, unavailable list rows, and invalid exact counts return typed
    `CONTAINERS_UNAVAILABLE` errors instead of zero/empty results. A missing
    container remains `NOT_FOUND`; chat maps failed reads to `AGENT_TOOL_FAILED`.
    Unit and mocked HTTP tests cover scope, field trimming, pagination, errors,
    and clarification/hostile-text turns. Live database/model validation remains
    pending.

    `get_container_summary` and `get_ledger_summary` are Tier 1 reads available

    const { AppError } = require('../../utils/errors');
    const { historySchema } = require('../validators/conversation.validator');
    const { emptyApprovalSchema, proposedToolResultSchema, proposalReferencesSchema } = require('../validators/proposal.validator');
    
    const unavailable = () => new AppError('Conversation history is unavailable. Please start a new conversation.', 503, 'AGENT_CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE');
    
    /** Only correlated, server-saved proposal exchanges can identify receipts.
     * User prose, other tool payloads and historical receipt arrays are inert.
     */
    function extractProposalReferences(history) {
      const parsed = historySchema.safeParse(history);
      if (!parsed.success) throw unavailable();
      const proposals = new Map();
      for (const turn of parsed.data) {
        for (let index = 1; index < turn.length - 1; index += 1) {
          const calls = turn[index].tool_calls;
          if (!calls) continue;
          for (let offset = 0; offset < calls.length; offset += 1) {
            const call = calls[offset];
            if (call.function.name !== 'mark_notification_read') continue;
            let args;
            let result;
            try {
              args = JSON.parse(call.function.arguments);
              result = JSON.parse(turn[index + offset + 1].content);
            } catch { throw unavailable(); }
            const payload = proposedToolResultSchema.safeParse(result);
            if (calls.length !== 1 || !emptyApprovalSchema.safeParse(args).success || !payload.success) throw unavailable();
            const proposal = payload.data.data.proposal;
            const previous = proposals.get(proposal.id);
            if (previous && JSON.stringify(previous) !== JSON.stringify(proposal)) throw unavailable();
            proposals.set(proposal.id, proposal);
          }
        }
      }
      const references = proposalReferencesSchema.safeParse([...proposals.values()]);
      if (!references.success) throw unavailable();
      return references.data;
    }
    
    module.exports = { extractProposalReferences };

          if (offset >= bytes.length) { controller.close(); return; }
          const end = split ? Math.min(bytes.length, offset + split) : bytes.length;
          controller.enqueue(bytes.subarray(offset, end));
          offset = end;
        },
      }), { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', ...headers } });
    }
    
    function parseEvents(text) {
      return text.trim().split('\n\n').map((frame) => {
        const [type, data] = frame.split('\n');
        return { type: type.slice(7), data: JSON.parse(data.slice(6)) };
      });
    }
    
    module.exports = { usage, chunk, frame, textChunks, toolChunks, sseResponse, parseEvents };

    function assertNotCancelled(signal) {

    module.exports = { assertNotCancelled };
    
    A successful first reply includes `data.conversation_id`, a server-generated
    UUID. Send that ID with a follow-up to resume the conversation:
    
    ```json
    { "message": "The London one.", "conversation_id": "<returned-uuid>" }
    ```
    
    Send `null` again to start over, or omit the field for a stateless request.
    Client-supplied messages/history, tool results, roles, and identity overrides
    remain rejected. The response contains text, turn metrics, the ID and an
    optional notification proposal; the saved transcript is never returned.
    The conversation ID is not sent to the model.
    
    Redis stores at most eight completed turns, with a 30-minute idle expiry
    refreshed after a successful turn. The active conversation retains the existing
    128 KiB message limit; old turns are removed as complete exchanges when room
    is needed. This is short-term context, not durable chat history. Stored data
    is bound to the authenticated user, membership, workspace, and role. An ID
    cannot carry admin history into a member request or cross workspace/user
    boundaries. Every request still traverses the existing auth/membership chain.
    
    The loop rebuilds the system instruction and reads current context on every
    turn. It uses old exchanges to interpret clarifications and instructs the
    model to refresh workspace facts through tools. Historical tool messages keep
    their untrusted-data envelopes; their call IDs are remapped to avoid collisions
    with new calls. Strict stored-message validation rejects system/developer
    messages, broken tool exchanges, oversized records, and unsupported tools.
    Conversation history never authorizes a write or approves a proposal.
    
    Atomic Redis scripts acquire a turn lease and save a completed transcript only
    while that lease still belongs to the request. Concurrent requests receive
    409 `AGENT_CONVERSATION_BUSY` before a model call. The lease expires after ten
    minutes; a late request cannot overwrite or release a newer request's lease.
    A lost lease or transcript expiry during a turn returns 409
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_CONFLICT`. Failed turns retain the previous transcript;
    failed first turns discard their unpublished record when cleanup is available.
    
    Unknown, expired, or differently scoped IDs return the same 404
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND`. Redis failure or corrupt history returns 503
    `AGENT_CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE`; history is never silently replaced with an
    empty conversation. Redis commands have a one-second deadline. An already
    submitted command may complete after that deadline; leases and records still
    expire. A persistence failure can occur after provider usage has been charged.
    Stateless requests remain available under the existing Redis-outage behavior.
    
    Unit tests cover real Lua scripts with ioredis-mock, storage failures, scope
    changes, lease races, history limits, clarification turns, and the real HTTP
    composition with mocked transports. Actual Redis expiry/atomicity and live
    model follow-up, prompt-injection, and numerical-fidelity evaluations remain
    integration/evaluation work.
    
    ## Internal read loop
    
    `runReadTurn({ data: { message }, context, provider })` in
    `services/read-loop.service.js` runs one fresh read-only turn. Server code
    supplies the authenticated context and the provider. Client data accepts only
    a text message; conversation history, roles, tool results, and workspace IDs
    are rejected. Each invocation starts with `get_my_context` and keeps its
    messages and authenticated identity local to that invocation.
    
    `runReadTurnWithHistory` is the internal stateful variant. It accepts validated
    server-owned history separately from client `data` and returns `{ reply,
    history }` to the conversation service for storage. Neither interface accepts
    history in the client's message object. Current tool/model-call limits apply
    per turn, excluding the exchanges restored from previous turns.
    
    The injected provider implements:
    
    ```js
    provider.chat({ messages, tools, trace })
    // -> { text: string | null, toolCalls: [{ id, name, arguments: string }], usage? }
    // usage: { promptTokens, completionTokens, totalTokens } | null
    ```
    
    Messages use chat-completion roles and correlated `tool_call_id` values.
    Tool definitions contain `name`, `description`, and the Zod `parameterSchema`;
    the provider adapter owns converting schemas to its wire format. Only the
    caller's permitted Tier 0/1 definitions are supplied by default. Explicit
    notification selection adds its proposal definition, handled by a separate
    proposal callback that cannot execute the write. Every read execution still
    passes through `executeReadTool` and the handler's permission checks.
    
    Tool messages wrap results in `{ kind: 'untrusted_tool_result', data }`, and
    the fixed system instruction treats their contents as data and forbids
    RPC permissions have integration coverage in
    `tests/integration/database/ranked-search.test.js` and
    `tests/integration/database/extended-ranked-search.test.js`. Run those suites
    with the real Postgres/PostgREST/Redis test stack and the updated schema.
    Unit tests mock RPC results and do not prove that the SQL or indexes work.

    +## Read status and continue the conversation
    +
    +Read a saved receipt without making a decision:
    +
    +```text
    +GET /v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/agent/proposals/:proposalId
    +```
    +
    +The route requires authentication, fresh active membership and the same
    +user/member/workspace/role scope as the proposal. It shares the per-user
    +agent rate limiter and returns `Cache-Control: no-store`. It never calls the
    +model, writes audit events, renews expiry, repairs an audit or executes an
    +action. A successful response uses the existing envelope:
    +
    +```json
    +{
    +  "data": {
    +    "proposal_id": "<proposal-uuid>",
    +    "tool": "mark_notification_read",
    +    "notification_id": "<notification-uuid>",
    +    "status": "executed",
    +    "expires_at": "<approval-expiry-ISO-timestamp>",
    +    "checked_at": "<server-check-ISO-timestamp>",
    +    "result": {
    +      "notification_id": "<notification-uuid>",
    +      "is_read": true,
    +      "read_at": "<stored-database-ISO-timestamp>"
    +    }
    +  }
    +}
    +```
    +
    +| Status | Meaning |
    +| --- | --- |
    +| `pending` | Awaiting approval or rejection. |
    +| `expired` | The approval deadline passed before execution was claimed. |
    +| `approval_pending` | Approval processing has started; no saved execution result. |
    +| `indeterminate` | Execution was claimed; the outcome is unconfirmed, possibly still processing. Never assume success/failure or repeat the action. |
    +| `rejection_pending` | Rejection processing has started; final auditing/storage is incomplete. |
    +| `rejected` | Rejected without execution. |
    +| `failed` | The proposal became stale or its conditional update was refused. |
    +| `audit_pending` | The mutation result was saved but final auditing/completion is unfinished. Repeating approval can finish this without repeating the write. |
    +| `executed` | The result and final audit are saved. |
    +
    +Only `audit_pending` and `executed` include `result`. Expiry does not erase a
    +recorded outcome. Missing, preparing or differently scoped records return
    +404; corrupt or unavailable storage returns 503. This endpoint reports a
    +past action, not the notification's current database state.
    +
    +When a conversation resumes, server code finds proposal cards only in validated,
    +correlated `mark_notification_read` call/result exchanges in retained history.
    +It ignores IDs in user/assistant prose, other tool payloads and old receipt
    +arrays. The server rechecks membership and compares each complete historical
    +card with its scoped Redis record, then adds fresh `action_receipts` to this
    +turn's initial `get_my_context` result, inside the untrusted-data envelope.
    +This does not offer another model-callable tool or restore notification selection.
    +
    +Refresh is bounded to eight unique cards; normal follow-ups start with at most
    +seven previous turns. Whole-turn eviction also bounds how long a proposal can
    +be refreshed. Receipts alone never carry a reference forward after its original
    +proposal exchange leaves history. A stateless request or new conversation has
    +an empty receipt array and does not discover proposals from other conversations.
    +
    +For a missing, changed or unreadable record, internal conversation context gets
    +only `{ proposal_id, status: "unavailable", checked_at }`, with no historical
    +target/result substituted. Membership failures stop the turn before the model
    +is invoked. Prompts require action claims to use this turn's fresh receipts,
    +never old cards/receipts or user claims of approval. JSON and SSE follow-ups use
    +the same refresh path; neither can execute a write.
    +
     ## Expiry, failures and audit

    // Only text comes from the client. Context and provider are server-owned.

    // Omit for a stateless turn; null starts a conversation; a UUID resumes it.

    }).strict();

    const { AppError } = require('../../utils/errors');
    const { historySchema } = require('../validators/conversation.validator');
    const { emptyApprovalSchema, proposedToolResultSchema, proposalReferencesSchema } = require('../validators/proposal.validator');
    
    const unavailable = () => new AppError('Conversation history is unavailable. Please start a new conversation.', 503, 'AGENT_CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE');
    
    /** Only correlated, server-saved proposal exchanges can identify receipts.
     * User prose, other tool payloads and historical receipt arrays are inert.
     */
    function extractProposalReferences(history) {
      const parsed = historySchema.safeParse(history);
      if (!parsed.success) throw unavailable();
      const proposals = new Map();
      for (const turn of parsed.data) {
        for (let index = 1; index < turn.length - 1; index += 1) {
          const calls = turn[index].tool_calls;
          if (!calls) continue;
          for (let offset = 0; offset < calls.length; offset += 1) {
            const call = calls[offset];
            if (call.function.name !== 'mark_notification_read') continue;
            let args;
            let result;
            try {
              args = JSON.parse(call.function.arguments);
              result = JSON.parse(turn[index + offset + 1].content);
            } catch { throw unavailable(); }
            const payload = proposedToolResultSchema.safeParse(result);
            if (calls.length !== 1 || !emptyApprovalSchema.safeParse(args).success || !payload.success) throw unavailable();
            const proposal = payload.data.data.proposal;
            const previous = proposals.get(proposal.id);
            if (previous && JSON.stringify(previous) !== JSON.stringify(proposal)) throw unavailable();
            proposals.set(proposal.id, proposal);
          }
        }
      }
      const references = proposalReferencesSchema.safeParse([...proposals.values()]);
      if (!references.success) throw unavailable();
      return references.data;
    }
    
    module.exports = { extractProposalReferences };

    // tests/setup.unit.js
    //
    // Runs via Jest's `setupFilesAfterEnv` for the "unit" project â€” AFTER the
    // test framework itself is initialised but BEFORE any test file's own
    // top-level code executes. This ordering matters: it's what lets us set
    // process.env here and have it already be in place by the time a test
    // file's `require('../../src/services/whatever.service')` transitively
    // pulls in config/supabase.js, which reads these vars at module-load
    // time and calls process.exit(1) if they're missing (see
    // config/supabase.js's top-level guard). A beforeAll() inside an
    // individual test file would run too late for that.
    //
    // Unit tests NEVER talk to real Postgres/Redis â€” every DB/Redis call is
    // mocked at the module level (see tests/mocks/*). These env vars exist
    // purely so config/supabase.js's startup guard and any code that reads
    // process.env.FRONTEND_URL / etc. don't crash before the mocks take
    // over.
    
    process.env.NODE_ENV = 'test';
    
    process.env.SUPABASE_URL = 'https://test.supabase.local';
    process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = 'test-service-role-key';
